thread.title: Broadcom-Qualcomm Drama Continues; Starboard Launches Campaign at Newell--ICYMI

author: thestreet.com
title: Broadcom-Qualcomm Drama Continues; Starboard Launches Campaign at Newell--ICYMI
text:
Amid the 900-point swings in the Dow on Friday , which capped one of the worst trading weeks since just after the financial crisis, there was major drama unfolding in the Broadcom ( AVGO ) -Qualcomm ( QCOM ) merger soap opera.
Like any good daytime television show, this battle's got a lot going for it in terms of intrigue. Both companies have strong-minded leaders and rich back stories of success and failure. There's love and desire, longing and disdain, and even a little ménage à trois.
OK, I've got your attention, don't I?
Broadcom's CEO Hock Tan is crying foul at Qualcomm's tactics, as his company presses forward with a hostile takeover of the mobile chipmaker. Tan had apparently wanted to negotiate with Qualcomm Chairman Dr. Paul Jacobs before the companies meet with proxy advisory firms Glass Lewis and ISS about dueling proposals at Qualcomm's upcoming annual meeting. Qualcomm apparently has other plans.
"I was astonished to hear that Qualcomm is not willing to meet until Tuesday -only after Qualcomm's and Broadcom's respective meetings with Glass Lewis and ISS," Tan said in a letter to Jacobs late Thursday . The Broadcom CEO urged Jacobs to hold talks Saturday or Sunday .
We've got the drama and intrigue covered now for the ménage à trois.
Qualcomm rejected the revised bid Thursday , saying the offer does not represent the value of its pending acquisition of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) , for the resolution of licensing disputes with Apple ( AAPL ) and for the opportunity to sell a new generation of technology for 5g wireless networks. Who's really the third wheel here?
It's pretty hard to avoid drama these days and when it comes to stock picking, sometimes it's not a bad idea to follow the drama.
To that end, take a look at Newell Brands ( NWL ) , home of Rubbermaid and other household products. Shares of Newell are down 3.5% to $26.95 after reports say activist investor Starboard Value will launch a proxy fight against the struggling company.
The company has been a bit of a laggard since its last earnings report in January, but does own valuable brands that have a place in today's consumer landscape.
If Starboard and founder Jeff Smith are successful in overthrowing the company's board, odds are the company could be in for a major spike. That is, if Starboard can conjure the same boardroom magic as it has brought to bear in past campaigns.
Smith has already been busy this year, launching four campaigns so far, two of which seek to overthrow entire boards of directors. His past successes include Darden ( DRI ) , which he successfully sculpted into a lean restaurant company and Yahoo! which he managed to push toward a sale after numerous unsuccessful attempts by other insurgents.
Looking to avoid the drama, TheStreet is out with its list of favorite dividend yielding stocks that could help insulate your portfolio as the market remain choppy.

Photo of the day: A proposed ownership change for a 109-year-old company
Makeup company L'Oréal is as storied as they come, tracing its beginning back to 1909 and a young chemist named Eugène Schueller ginning up potions for Parisian hairdressers. But with such a long history, the company has encountered its ups and downs in business and numerous owners. On Friday , Jean-Paul Agon, now CEO of the 109-year-old company, is seeking to bring 100% ownership of the French company under one roof for the first time since 1974. Agon said his company was willing and able to buy back the roughly 23% of his company that is owned by fellow French multinational Nestle. Nestle bought into L'Oréal at the request of Liliane Bettencourt, the daughter of the founder, to prevent the French state's intervention in the company.
